results.question: Which hum/sung-melody note transcriber and which monophonic F0 tracker have clean code and weights licenses, run on Apple Silicon under a current Python, and have published humming or singing benchmarks (note-level onset/offset F1 for Basic Pitch against SOME/ROSVOT and F0+HMM pipelines)?
results.finding:
No candidate meets all three conditions. No published humming benchmark reports note-level onset+offset F1 for Basic Pitch against SOME, GAME, ROSVOT, or any F0+HMM pipeline.

BENCHMARKS FOUND
(1) HumTrans paper (arXiv 2309.09623).
- Tested only VOCANO, Sheet Sage, MIR-ST500 and JDC-STP.
- Its eval script (shansongliu/HumTrans calc_transcription_eval_metric.py) uses mir_eval precision_recall_f1_overlap with offset_ratio=None, so offsets are ignored. Onset tolerance is 50 ms, pitch tolerance is 1 cent on integer MIDI, and scoring is octave-invariant.
- F1 on the test set: VOCANO 3.35, Sheet Sage 3.01, MIR-ST500 5.76, JDC-STP 5.67. The authors call this 'far from satisfactory'.
- Licenses: dataset CC BY-NC 4.0 (HF dadinghh2/HumTrans); the eval repo has no license.

(2) Dynamic HumTrans (arXiv 2410.05455; course-project repo shubham-gupta-30/humming_transcription, unlicensed, checkpoints not uploaded).
- This is the only humming result that includes Basic Pitch. It scores onset+pitch F1, still with no offset.
- Basic Pitch: 0.434 octave-invariant, 0.268 octave-aware. Comparisons: MIR-ST500 0.604/0.361, VOCANO 0.564/0.341, JDC-STP 0.490/0.286, the authors' CNN 0.673/0.651.
- These numbers use the authors' relabelled onsets; they report that HumTrans onset/offset labels are misaligned.

(3) ROSVOT's paper (ACL 2024).
- Reports COnPOff F 77.4 clean / 77.0 noisy on Mandarin singing (M4Singer subsets).
- Compared only against TONY, VOCANO, MusicYOLO and Yong et al.; no humming data.

(4) lars76/pitch-benchmark v2.1 (MIT; run by SwiftF0's own author; eval data CC BY-NC-SA).
- Frame-level pitch F1@50c only, not notes.
- Vocadito solo singing: RMVPE 0.862, SwiftF0 0.847, TorchCREPE 0.789, FCPE 0.786, CREPE 0.781, PESTO 0.759, pYIN 0.653, Basic Pitch 0.638 (note output).
- Overall: SwiftF0 0.781 (tied with RMVPE 0.768), FCPE 0.728, CREPE 0.689, PESTO 0.680, Basic Pitch 0.557, pYIN 0.506.

PER-CANDIDATE STATUS
Basic Pitch
- Apache-2.0 for code and bundled weights.
- Last release 0.4.0 on 2024-08-16. Main has unreleased fixes from 2025-11, including note truncation (#179).
- README: on M1 'we currently only support python version 3.10'.
- Issue #203 (2026-09-08): basic-pitch==0.4.0 cannot be resolved on macOS arm64 with Python 3.12, because tensorflow-macos<2.15.1 has no cp312 wheel.
- Ships CoreML, ONNX, TFLite and TF models.

SOME and GAME
- SOME: MIT code; released weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (stated in release notes); ONNX export.
- Its successor openvpi/GAME: MIT code; v1.0.3 on 2026-03-09 with ONNX models; tested on Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.8. Its weights are also CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

ROSVOT
- MIT code. Weights are on Google Drive with no license, were trained only on M4Singer (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), and bundle RMVPE.
- Tested on Python 3.9 / torch 2.1.1 / CUDA 11.8. Last push 2024-11.

librosa pYIN
- ISC license, no weights.
- librosa 1.0.0 (2026-08-11) requires Python >=3.12. Runs on CPU.

CREPE
- MIT. Weights come from the repo's models branch.
- Training data includes MedleyDB (non-commercial) and others.
- Runs on TF/Keras.

torchcrepe
- 0.0.24 (2025-05), MIT. Bundles full.pth and tiny.pth converted from CREPE.
- MPS is not documented.

FCPE
- MIT repo with a bundled fcpe_c_v001.pt; its training data is not stated.
- The paper's DDSP-200K model on HF ChiTu/FCPE is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
- torchfcpe 0.0.4 (2024-03).

PESTO
- LGPL-3.0 code and in-repo weights; self-supervised on MIR-1K.
- pesto-pitch 2.0.1; ONNX and TorchScript export.

RMVPE
- Official Dream-High/RMVPE is Apache-2.0 but ships no weights.
- The weights people actually use are yxlllc/RMVPE (no license; trained on MIR-1K + PTDB + M4Singer vocoder data) or RVC's rmvpe.pt (HF lj1995 repo tagged MIT, provenance unstated).

SwiftF0 (new candidate, from the same author as the benchmark)
- 0.3.0 on 2026-09-25. MIT code and bundled ONNX model; needs only numpy and onnxruntime.
- Python 3.8-3.14. Includes segment_notes() and MIDI export.
- Trained on the author's CC BY-NC-SA research dataset.
results.corrected_value:
F0 tracker for A7: SwiftF0 (MIT, ONNX, Python up to 3.14), with librosa pYIN (ISC, no weights) as a weights-free cross-check. torchcrepe and PESTO are secondary options. Note transcriber for A4: no option is clean, current and humming-benchmarked.
- Basic Pitch is the only one with a humming number (onset+pitch F1 0.27-0.43, no offset). It needs Python 3.10 or a --no-deps CoreML/ONNX workaround on macOS.
- SOME, GAME and ROSVOT fail the weights-license test.
- Ticket: build a local benchmark on Jon's own hums plus HumTrans (CC BY-NC, personal evaluation only). Score COn/COnP/COnPOff with mir_eval, comparing Basic Pitch against SwiftF0.segment_notes and pYIN with HMM note segmentation.

results.weights_license: Basic Pitch Apache-2.0 (bundled). SOME and GAME CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. ROSVOT unlicensed, trained on non-commercial M4Singer. pYIN has no weights. CREPE/torchcrepe MIT-labelled but trained partly on non-commercial MedleyDB. FCPE: bundled v001 MIT, DDSP-200K CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. PESTO LGPL-3.0. RMVPE: no clean official weights. SwiftF0: MIT-labelled ONNX trained on a CC BY-NC-SA dataset.

results.hardware_notes: Basic Pitch runs through CoreML by default on macOS, with ONNX optional. Official Apple Silicon support is Python 3.10 only; 3.12 installs fail (#203). SwiftF0 runs through ONNX Runtime on CPU (vendor-claimed 180x real time on one core). PESTO exports to ONNX and TorchScript. GAME has released ONNX models. torchcrepe, FCPE and ROSVOT are PyTorch, and MPS is not documented for any of them; ROSVOT targets CUDA 11.8. librosa 1.0 needs Python >=3.12. All speed numbers are vendor-claimed.

results.question: Can a YuE2 caller pass its own melody/chord ABC plus lyrics without SheetSage2? Which ABC subset is accepted, how are lyrics bound to bars, does cot='melody' keep pitches exactly, what is the maximum length, which languages are supported, and do SheetSage2/MERT2 load on this path?
results.finding:
Yes. Current main (commit 1647252, 2026-10-06; package yue2-infer 0.1.6) accepts a user score through YuE2Pipeline(...)(style=, lyrics=, abc=, cot='full'|'melody'). The CLI equivalent is `yue2 generate --abc-file`. protocol.SongRequest rejects abc when cot='off'. pipeline.plan() returns the supplied ABC unchanged as the plan: it is tokenized and inserted as an [ABC_START] abc [ABC_END][MUSIC_START] prefix, with zero planner tokens, and the model then generates semantic codes from it. The runtime does not validate the ABC itself; only the skill helper (skills/yue2-music/scripts/abc_tools.py) does.

(1) ABC SUBSET ('bounded native dialect')
- Header: fixed X:1 and blank T:. Then M: as an explicit fraction, L:1/<power of 2> (L:1/32 is typical), and a single integer Q:1/4=<BPM>.
- Exactly two monophonic voices, 'V: Vocal' and 'V: Ins'. Chord symbols go only in Vocal.
- Music comes in groups of 1-4 bars, each a V: Vocal block followed by a V: Ins block. % verse / % chorus comments mark sections.
- Meter and key changes are allowed only at group boundaries, in both voices; an inline [K:] is also allowed.
- Duration multipliers 1/2/3/4/6/8/12/16/24/32/48, ties, accidentals, and Z rests.
- Every bar must sum exactly to the meter, so pickup bars must be padded with rests.
- Rejected: tuplets (support PR #185 is still open), grace notes, chords/stacks, repeats, endings, slurs, broken rhythm, decorations, w: lyric lines, tempo changes, and non-native chord qualities.
- The native chord vocabulary is listed in references/abc-editing.md.

(2) LYRIC BINDING
- There is no syllable-to-note or bar binding channel. Lyrics are free text with [Verse]/[Chorus] tags placed in the text condition.
- The docs say to align section order and syllable counts with the score by hand, to keep any alignment in sidecar files, and never to add w: fields.

(3) EXACTNESS
- Not guaranteed. The skill docs say the helper does not 'force the generator to follow the score', and the paper says the supplied score is a fixed prefix while audio is regenerated.
- Measured edit adherence on edited model-generated scores (docs/benchmarks.md): exact target-pitch accuracy 84.17% for melody edits; unedited melody agreement 93-94%; rhythm 73.43%; tempo Acc2 95.68%.
- cot='melody' does not strip chord symbols; the caller must remove them.
- No adherence figure exists for hand-written ABC.

(4) LENGTH
- Context is 24,576 tokens. Semantic codes run at 25 Hz with max_tokens 9000 by default, which is 360 s; benchmarks.md refers to a 'six-minute cap'.
- sampling.py raises an error if prefix + budget > 24576. The supplied ABC and lyrics count toward the prefix.
- The planner's own ABC is capped at 4096 tokens. yue2.cpp reports a 2239-token score for a 212 s song.
- No bar limit is documented.

(5) LANGUAGES
- The HF card lists language zh, en. WildSongBench has 94 Chinese and 98 English prompts.
- No other language is officially claimed; audio.cpp lists yue2 as 'en'.

(6) SHEETSAGE2 / MERT2
- Not loaded. src/yue2 has no SheetSage or MERT import, and pyproject depends only on torch, transformers, hf-hub, safetensors, tiktoken, numpy, soundfile and accelerate.
- README: 'SheetSage2 runs in a separate environment'; MERT is only SheetSage2's encoder.

LICENSE CAVEAT
- YuE2-3B, YuE2-Vae and YuE2-Vae-legacy weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (not Apache-2.0 like YuE v1). They carry a 2026-09-16 'individual creator permission'.
- SheetSage2 and MERT-v2 are CC BY-NC 4.0 without that permission.
results.corrected_value: The user-ABC path exists and is native: abc= with cot='full' or 'melody'. It is conditioning, not exact rendering; edit-adherence evidence is about 84% pitch accuracy. The converter ticket must emit the strict native two-voice dialect: fixed header, single integer tempo, full bars only, no tuplets, no pickup bars, sections as % comments. Lyrics are bound only by matching section tags and order. Length is at most about 6 min. Languages: Chinese and English only.
results.code_license: Apache-2.0 for the repository code and the yue2-music skill (since PR #159, 2026-09-10). Third-party MIT notices cover the Oobleck VAE and SnakeBeta.
results.weights_license: YuE2-3B, YuE2-Vae and YuE2-Vae-legacy: CC BY-NC 4.0 plus an additional individual-creator permission (MODEL_LICENSE, 2026-09-16), not gated. Companies need a separate commercial license. SheetSage2 and MERT-v2-FullSong/30s: CC BY-NC 4.0 with no creator permission.
results.output_rights: Under MODEL_LICENSE, personal users, content creators and musicians 'acting in an individual capacity' may generate outputs and 'publish, distribute, sell, license or otherwise monetize' them without fees, subject to responsible-use conditions. 'Generated outputs are not subject to the model weights' NonCommercial restriction solely because they were generated with YuE2.' This does not authorize commercial use of the weights by companies, and it does not allow redistributing or selling the weights.
results.hardware_notes: Officially Linux, Python 3.12 (3.10+), with a BF16-capable NVIDIA GPU of 24 GB. The user-ABC path adds no models. SheetSage2, if used, runs in its own Python 3.10/3.11 environment with torch 2.8.0 and FFmpeg 6.1.

results.question: What VRAM, host RAM, OS and GPU/driver does YuE2-3B plus YuE2-Vae need for full-context generation through to decode? Does it fit 16 GB cards, and does it run on native Windows or WSL2?
results.finding:
Row A4's 'CONFIRMED 24 GB' is a vendor recommendation, not a measured floor. The YuE2-3B card says 'Use a 24GB GPU and 24GB available host RAM; maximum-context testing peaked at 14.08 GiB.'

MEASURED VRAM (vendor, RTX 4090, 32 warm runs per mode, NVML full-run GPU peak)
- 11.18 GiB for cot=full, 11.02 for melody, 11.09 for off. A 3.6-min song takes 71 s.
- 10.34 GiB on an H800.

16 GB CARDS (4060 Ti 16 GB / 4080 / 5070 Ti)
- No official validation and no official reports on the PyTorch path.
- The pipeline caps PyTorch at min(budget-2, total-2) GiB, so about 14 GiB on a 16 GB card. That makes the 14.08 GiB max-context NVML peak borderline.
- Built-in levers: --budget <=12 (switches VAE tiles to 512), --quantization fp8, --offload-ar.
- Community low-VRAM PRs are unmerged: #164 (8 GB RTX 3060 Ti) and #174 (6-8 GB).
- The GGUF ports fit easily: audio.cpp reports a peak of 12.5 GiB BF16, 8.9 GiB Q8 and 7.8 GiB Q4 on an RTX 5090. yue2.cpp reports 5.8 GB for a 65 s song in Q8 at full context.

NATIVE WINDOWS: not supported, and broken on current main with official wheels.
- The torch 2.10.0 Windows wheel on PyPI is CPU-only (114 MB), so `pip install .` gives CPU torch. You need the download.pytorch.org cu128 or cu130 index.
- On the official Windows torch 2.10.0 wheels, FlashAttention is a stub, and the hasattr check in cuda_graph.py makes generation fail. Fix PR #166 is still open; main still has the hasattr check.
- Issue #209 (Windows 11, RTX 5090, torch 2.10.0+cu130, driver 616.56): the NAR stage falls back to MATH SDPA, about 6x slower and +7 GB VRAM. Whole-GPU peak is 22.1 GB versus 14.7 GB with a cuDNN workaround.
- The vLLM extra (vllm==0.19.0, triton==3.6.0) has manylinux wheels only.

WSL2: the officially supported Linux path, with caveats.
- NVIDIA's guide says to install only the Windows driver ('Do not install any Linux display driver in WSL') and supports Pascal or newer GPUs in WDDM mode.
- Pinned system memory is limited and unified memory is not available.
- Microsoft's WSL2 VM defaults to memory = 50% of Windows RAM. A 32 GB Windows box therefore gives about 16 GB, below the 24 GB host-RAM recommendation, so set .wslconfig memory.
- No YuE2 maintainer statement on WSL2 was found.

GPU AND DRIVER
- pyproject pins torch==2.10.0. The PyPI Linux x86_64 wheel is a CUDA 12.8 build (nvidia-*-cu12 12.8.x).
- PyTorch RELEASE.md: 2.10 stable CUDA 12.6/12.8, experimental 13.0. 2.11 stable 12.6/12.8/13.0. 2.12 and later stable 12.6/13.0, with no 12.8.
- So for Blackwell sm_120: cu128 with torch <=2.11 needs driver >=570.26 on Linux or >=570.65 on Windows; cu130 needs R580+. The statement in the question is confirmed.
- Raising torch to >=2.13 to fix the MPS bug (PR #190) would push Blackwell users onto cu130/R580+.
- BF16 is required (the code raises if torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported() is False). Native BF16 tensor cores and FlashAttention mean Ampere (RTX 30xx) or newer in practice. Turing/T4 was seen only through GGUF ports, for example a community Colab T4 audio.cpp notebook.
results.corrected_value:
A4 hardware row:
- Officially: Linux, a 24 GB BF16 NVIDIA GPU, and 24 GB host RAM.
- Vendor-measured peak 11.2 GiB typical, 14.1 GiB at maximum context. 16 GB cards are plausible but unvalidated on the PyTorch path (use --budget, fp8 or offload), and comfortable through the GGUF ports.
- Native Windows needs patches (#166, plus the #209 workaround) and a manual CUDA torch wheel.
- WSL2 with the Windows NVIDIA driver is the practical route on a Windows box, provided .wslconfig memory is raised to 24 GB or more.
- Driver: >=570.26 on Linux or >=570.65 on Windows for the default cu128 wheel; R580+ for cu130.
results.code_license: Apache-2.0 for the YuE2 inference code. GGUF ports: audio.cpp Apache-2.0, yue2.cpp MIT.
results.weights_license: CC BY-NC 4.0 plus the individual-creator permission (MODEL_LICENSE).
results.output_rights: Same as GAP-02: individuals may monetize outputs; companies need a commercial license.
results.hardware_notes: Vendor-measured on RTX 4090/H800, not independently reproduced. The Windows numbers come from community issue #209. The GGUF VRAM numbers are claimed by the port authors. The 24 GB host-RAM figure is a vendor recommendation; WSL2 defaults to 50% of host RAM.

results.question: Can a non-ACE vocal song engine credibly run on the M5 Pro through the yue2.cpp Metal port, the MiniMax Music 3 MLX/GGUF ports, or the HeartMuLa MLX port? Are YuE issues #176 and #187 fixed upstream?
results.finding:
Several Metal-capable non-ACE ports exist, so a no-CUDA fallback does not have to be ACE-only. None has published Metal parity evidence against the PyTorch reference, and the official PyTorch MPS path has open bugs.

(a) yue2.cpp: https://github.com/ServeurpersoCom/yue2.cpp
- MIT code. Created 2026-09-12; last commit 2026-10-08 (c893629).
- Implements the score path: the request's abc and cot fields; 'Non-empty [abc] replaces the planning stage: the score is tokenized into the prefix as is'; cot melody/full/off.
- The README says 'macOS auto-enables Metal' but headlines 'Runs on CPU, CUDA, Vulkan'.
- Parity: 24 tests against the torch reference loaded from the checkpoint's own modeling code, all green on CUDA0 and CPU only (LM rel-RMS about 1-3e-3; NAR cosine harness). No Metal logs. No issues mention Metal.
- GGUFs: HF Serveurperso/YuE2-GGUF, CC BY-NC 4.0; the card does not restate the YuE2 creator permission.
- Related: audio.cpp (0xShug0, Apache-2.0, v0.9.1 on 2026-10-07) also runs YuE2 with ABC conditioning (cot=melody, abc_file) and NAR/VAE parity probes. Its README says the Metal backend is 'intended for portability and testing... performance and model coverage may be lower'. GGUF audio-cpp/Yue2-3B-GGUF is CC BY-NC 4.0.
- Only community evidence of YuE2 on Metal: Riff (Flip-Engineering, MIT, built on audio.cpp's Metal engine with Q4) self-reports 12-30 s M4 previews at about 2.7 GiB and fresh generation at 10.41 GB.

(b) MiniMax Music 3
- Upstream (MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-Music3) is CUDA-only; the elishabjm port notes 'CPU and MPS are not supported'.
- audio.cpp GGUF (audio-cpp/MiniMax-Music3-GGUF, LICENSE included) publishes only RTX 5090 numbers for 30 s: 9.8 GiB Q4 mix, 13.4 GiB Q8, 19.4 GiB BF16. 'Memory usage remains an active optimization target' for longer songs; no Metal measurement.
- vanch007/mlx-minimax-music3: v0.1.0, last commit 2026-08-14; distributed under the Community License. Uses 13.2 GiB of 8-bit weights; a 10-second generation peaked at 23.34 GiB MLX memory on an M3 Max 128 GB; 'not been validated on lower-memory Macs'.
- appautomaton/mlx-minimax-music3: MIT code, pre-alpha; dense checkpoint 26.56 GiB; 'long-form generation... remain in progress'.
- Against the M5 Pro's 37.44 GiB Metal working set: 10-30 s clips fit, full songs are unmeasured.
- License pass-through: yes. The ports ship the MiniMax-Music3 Community License unchanged.

(c) HeartMuLa MLX: Acelogic/heartlib-mlx
- No LICENSE file, so GitHub detects no license. But pyproject.toml and the README badge declare Apache-2.0.
- Last commit 2026-01-20; recommends 32 GB+ unified memory.
- Upstream HeartMuLa code and weights are Apache-2.0.
- A cleaner route is audio.cpp's heartmula family (Apache-2.0 weights, marked commercial 'Yes'), which uses the same Metal backend; also unmeasured on Mac.

YuE issue #176 (MPS BF16 causal SDPA leaks future keys under torch <=2.12.1)
- Still OPEN.
- The upstream fix is in PyTorch 2.13.0 (pytorch#195910). A community run on an M4 Pro with torch 2.14.0 overriding the pin shows correct results.
- The pin-raise PR #190 (torch>=2.13.0) is OPEN, and main still pins torch==2.10.0.

YuE #187 (Metal driver memory grows to 68-82 GiB at about 9k tokens; logits go non-finite)
- An OPEN, unmerged PR. No MPS commits have landed on main since 2026-09-10.
- The official MPS path is therefore not usable for full-length songs without patches.
results.corrected_value:
Without CUDA, Mac non-ACE options exist but none is verified:
- YuE2 through audio.cpp or yue2.cpp on Metal, with GGUF Q8 at about 4-10 GB and the ABC path implemented. Needs Metal parity and listening tests before it counts.
- HeartMuLa through audio.cpp (Apache-2.0 weights).
- MiniMax Music 3 through MLX 8-bit (23 GiB for 10 s; full-length songs unmeasured).
- The official YuE2 PyTorch MPS path stays blocked until #176 (torch >=2.13) and #187 are resolved upstream or patched locally.

MiniMax-Music3 Community License: copyright notice, AUP, 'MiniMax-Music3' shown in a commercial product's UI, written authorization above USD 20M yearly revenue, safeguards when offered to third parties. The Mac data volume has only about 8.5 GiB free, but YuE2 Q8 GGUFs total about 4.3 GB plus about 0.9 GB optional MERT, while MiniMax MLX 8-bit is about 13.2 GiB and dense about 26.6 GiB. So disk is a blocker for MiniMax on the Mac.

new_discoveries: YuE2-3B and both YuE2 VAEs are CC BY-NC 4.0, not Apache-2.0 like YuE v1. A 2026-09-16 MODEL_LICENSE grant lets individual creators monetize outputs, but the weights cannot be used commercially by companies. If AURA becomes an Island Development Crew product, or is distributed so others can generate with it, a commercial license from MAP (ryuanab@connect.ust.hk) is needed. SheetSage2 and MERT-v2 are CC BY-NC 4.0 with no creator permission.

YuE2 user-ABC is a native, documented path: abc= plus cot full or melody. It accepts only a strict two-voice dialect: no tuplets (PR #185 open), no pickup bars, a single integer tempo. There is no lyric-to-note binding channel, and length is capped at about 6 minutes (9000 semantic tokens at 25 Hz). Supported languages are zh and en. The MelodySpec-to-ABC converter must target this dialect, and the lyric syllable plan must be stored as a sidecar.

Native Windows YuE2 does not work out of the box on main. The PyPI torch 2.10.0 Windows wheel is CPU-only; the FlashAttention stub breaks generation (PR #166 open); and the NAR MATH-SDPA fallback costs about 6x speed and +7 GB VRAM (#209). On a Windows box, plan on WSL2, and raise .wslconfig memory because the default is 50% of RAM.

Official YuE2 on Apple MPS remains blocked. #176 (BF16 causal SDPA bug, fixed only in torch >=2.13) and #187 (Metal memory runaway at about 9k tokens) are both open, and the pin-raise PR #190 is unmerged. Raising torch to >=2.12 would also force CUDA 13 / R580+ drivers for Blackwell, because PyTorch dropped the cu128 builds.

audio.cpp (Apache-2.0, v0.9.1, 2026-10-07) is one native ggml runtime with CUDA, Vulkan, HIP and Metal backends. It runs YuE2 (with ABC conditioning and LoRA), HeartMuLa, MiniMax Music 3, SheetSage2, MuScriptor and ACE-Step. It could be AURA's cross-machine engine layer, but Metal has no parity data. yue2.cpp (MIT) is a dedicated alternative with ABC, continuation, LoRA stacking and a WebUI.

HeartMuLa (heartlib) code and weights are Apache-2.0, so it is the only non-ACE open vocal song model found with permissive weights. Vendor-reported WildSongBench SongBench Avg: HeartMuLa 6.25, ACE-Step 1.5 6.01, MiniMax Music 3 6.28, YuE2 6.73 (YuE2 authors' benchmark). It is a strong license-clean second engine candidate.

Prior-art studios that overlap AURA's scope: Ruach Studio (AGPL-3.0, on yue2.cpp, with score-first ABC/MIDI, stems, LoRA training and DAW export; Linux and 24 GB NVIDIA), Riff (MIT, Apple Silicon Metal via audio.cpp), and Remiqora (MIT, YuE2 + MuScriptor + ACE-Step + Demucs, per the audio.cpp README). Review them before building from scratch; the AGPL code cannot be mixed into a permissively licensed AURA.

openvpi/GAME (2026-03, the successor to SOME) has released ONNX models and does note-word alignment, but its weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. SOME's weights are also CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Neither can be a license-clean A4 transcriber.

SwiftF0 0.3.0 (2026-09-25) has MIT code and a bundled ONNX model, 14k params, Python 3.8-3.14, with built-in segment_notes() and MIDI export. It tops its author's 19-tracker benchmark, statistically tied with RMVPE. It is the best licensed, Mac-friendly F0 candidate for the A7 melody-adherence score, though its training data is CC BY-NC-SA.

librosa 1.0.0 (2026-08-11) requires Python >=3.12, while Basic Pitch 0.4.0 cannot install on macOS with Python >=3.12 (issue #203). A Basic Pitch plus librosa environment on the Mac therefore needs Python 3.10 or a --no-deps CoreML/ONNX install.

MuScriptor (Kyutai/Mirelo, ISMIR 2026) is a multi-instrument audio-to-MIDI model with MIT code and official MPS support. Its weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 and auto-gated, so it is not clean for stems-to-MIDI.

VocalParse (arXiv 2605.04613, HF ngoctham/VocalParse, Apache-2.0, based on Qwen3-ASR-1.7B) is a 2026 singing-transcription LALM. It has not been benchmarked on humming; it is an unverified lead for the A4 transcriber.

results.question: What exactly does the 'Individual creator permission' in YuE's GitHub MODEL_LICENSE (2026-09-16) allow? Does it cover licensing output songs to IDC LLC or using them on Sabbath Echo, does a single-member LLC count as a company, is it revocable, which text governs against the plain CC BY-NC on Hugging Face, and has the YuE team published an answer, a contact or terms?
results.finding:
The current MODEL_LICENSE text (commit cbb3b060, 2026-09-16 14:48Z) grants the permission to 'personal users, content creators and musicians acting in an individual capacity'. They may use the weights free of charge to generate outputs and 'publish, distribute, sell, license or otherwise monetize those outputs', and 'This includes distributing or licensing their outputs to clients and publishing them on commercial platforms.' The licensors 'waive the NonCommercial restriction to the extent necessary'. The text also states that outputs are 'not subject to the model weights' NonCommercial restriction solely because they were generated with YuE2'. The permission excludes companies: 'does not authorize commercial use of the model weights by companies'. Companies are sent to a commercial license.

(1) Licensing a song to IDC LLC: the text allows licensing outputs to clients. A song Jon generates as an individual and then licenses to the LLC therefore falls within the literal wording. Generation that is LLC work (directed by IDC, for an IDC venture such as Sabbath Echo, or run as company infrastructure) is 'commercial use of the model weights by companies', which the permission does not cover. 'Individual capacity' is not defined.

(2) Single-member LLC: not addressed anywhere. CC's own FAQ says NonCommercial 'does not turn on the type of user', but this extra permission does turn on the user type (individual versus company), so the CC reasoning does not settle it. Unresolved.

(3) Revocability: the CC BY-NC 4.0 grant is 'irrevocable' (Sec. 2(a)(1)). The extra permission has no revocability or irrevocability language, and responsible use is 'a condition' of it. The text says it does 'not restrict rights already granted under CC BY-NC 4.0, Apache 2.0 or earlier grants of additional permission'. That wording preserves the broader first version (commit 6c639ab8, four minutes earlier), which covered academic users too. Conflict with Hugging Face: there is no true conflict, because the permission is expressly 'In addition to' CC BY-NC, and the CC FAQ says licensors may grant extra permissions. However, the Hugging Face LICENSE for YuE2-3B, YuE2-Vae and YuE2-Vae-legacy is plain CC BY-NC with no creator permission and has not been updated since the 2026-09-09 release, and the model card says 'Weights: CC BY-NC 4.0 (LICENSE)'. Outside the permission's scope, CC BY-NC governs. The two contact points also differ: MODEL_LICENSE names ryuanab@connect.ust.hk, while the README Contact section, updated 2026-09-17 in commit bd90e4cc, lists 'Licensing inquiries: lauryliuyang@hkgai.org'.

(4) Public answers: none on LLCs or companies. Issue #189 (2026-09-16, individual commercial license) has only a non-maintainer reply, which predates or ignores the permission. In issue #177 a collaborator said only 'See our updated license description in Readme'. Issue #219 (opened 2026-10-09 by a sole trader asking for commercial terms) has no reply. No commercial price or terms are published; there is only a 'contact us'.
results.corrected_value: The individual lane is supported by the text. LLC-directed generation, including Sabbath Echo work, is not covered without a commercial license, and the single-member-LLC question is unanswered by the licensors. Get written confirmation from lauryliuyang@hkgai.org and ryuanab@connect.ust.hk before any LLC work runs on YuE2. Until then, run LLC work on Apache-2.0 YuE1, MIT ACE-Step 1.5 or MiniMax Music 3 (community license). This is not legal advice.
results.code_license: Apache-2.0 (first-party code, agent skill, docs); third-party MIT notices (stable-audio-tools, SnakeBeta)
results.weights_license: CC BY-NC 4.0 on Hugging Face and GitHub; the GitHub MODEL_LICENSE alone adds the 2026-09-16 individual-creator permission (not mirrored in the HF LICENSE files); not gated
results.output_rights: Individuals acting in an individual capacity may sell or license outputs, including to clients, with no fees or royalties; credit is optional; responsible-use condition. Companies need a separate commercial license, with no published terms.
results.hardware_notes: Official: Linux, Python 3.12, NVIDIA GPU with BF16 and 24 GB VRAM. The code auto-selects MPS (src/yue2/pipeline.py) and has an MPS attention fallback (modeling_yue2.py), but Apple Silicon is not documented as supported, so treat it as unofficial and untested.

results.question: Which v1 engines output separate vocal/accompaniment tracks natively (YuE2 dual-track? ACE-Step 1.5 lego/complete? MiniMax Music 3?), and does the original Demucs v4 release state a license that covers its pretrained checkpoints?
results.finding:
YuE2: no native stems. YuE1's dual-track design was dropped. The YuE2 paper describes one AR-NAR Mixture-of-Transformers that produces an ABC score, then one 25 Hz MERT2 semantic token stream ('a single 25-H[z]' stream), then 25 Hz latents for one 48 kHz stereo VAE decode. In the code, 'dual' means a dual attention/MLP inside the MoT, not two audio tracks. save_artifacts() writes a single audio.flac plus score.abc, plan.json, semantic/prefix .npy and latent.npy (docs/generation.md; storage.py lists audio.flac as the only audio). The score has separate Vocal and Ins voices, which are symbolic only. The instrumental workflow moves the vocal melody into the Ins part before rendering.

YuE1 (YuE-v1 branch): it does output separate tracks. infer.py writes '_vtrack' and '_itrack' token files, decodes vocoder stems 'vtrack.mp3' and 'itrack.mp3', and then sums them into a mix. YuE1 weights are Apache-2.0 on Hugging Face.

ACE-Step 1.5: there is no stem output from text2music. The base-model-only tasks are: lego, 'Generate the {TRACK_NAME} track based on the audio context:' (12 track names including vocals and backing_vocals); extract, 'Extract/isolate a specific instrument track from mixed audio'; and complete, which adds 'mixed accompaniment' to a single track such as an a cappella vocal. The docs do not say outright that lego returns only the new part. Two strong signals say it does: the official issue #117 workflow ('Layer the generated track over the source audio'), and the official ACE-Step-DAW, which places lego results as separate 'Stems (AI)' track clips. So a generated part can be obtained on its own (medium confidence). Two caveats apply. Timing drift was reported (#117, fixed by PR #810). Issue #1286 found that LM-generated codes overrode src_audio in lego and complete, and the interim fix #1287 keeps those tasks DiT-first.

MiniMax Music 3 (open weights): a single 32 kHz 16-bit stereo WAV with no track outputs. The MiniMax API returns one data.audio payload, and its only related option is is_instrumental.

Demucs v4: the repository LICENSE is MIT; it was CC BY-NC until commit 25dada5a on 2020-04-13. The v4 README and release notes never state a separate license for the checkpoints, which download from dl.fbaipublicfiles.com. The author, adefossez, stated in the official issues that the checkpoints are not MIT-licensed. In #327 (2022-05-23): 'The model weights are not covered by the MIT license, and are provided only for scientific purposes'. In #384 (2022-09-29): weights are 'research artefacts' 'only for personal / research usage' because MUSDB is research-only. In #508 (2023-08-02): 'Weights are provided for research purpose!'. On 2026-08-31 he committed 'Remove license from model card' to the Hugging Face repos (adefossez/HTDemucs was uploaded 2026-07-11 with license: mit) and removed 'license: mit' from tools/export_hf.py. That is why the safetensors carry no license field.
results.corrected_value: Native generation-time stems: only YuE1 (2 stems, Apache-2.0, lower quality: SongBench Avg 4.92 versus 6.73 for YuE2 in the YuE2 paper). ACE-Step 1.5 base can generate a part on its own (lego) or isolate one generatively (extract) under MIT weights. YuE2 and MiniMax Music 3 output a single mix only. Demucs checkpoints are research/personal-only according to the author, so they belong on the release-blocker list as 'non-commercial (author statement)' rather than 'unknown'.
results.code_license: YuE2 Apache-2.0; YuE1 Apache-2.0; ACE-Step 1.5 MIT; MiniMax-Music3 code in the same community license; Demucs code MIT
results.weights_license: YuE2 CC BY-NC 4.0 (+ GitHub creator permission); YuE1 Apache-2.0; ACE-Step 1.5 base/xl-base MIT; MiniMax-Music3 Community License (commercial OK, 'MiniMax-Music3' must be shown in the UI of commercial products, written authorization needed above US$20M yearly revenue, safeguards if offered to third parties); Demucs checkpoints research/personal-only per author, and the HF license tag was removed on 2026-08-31
results.output_rights: MiniMax AUP item 11 requires clear disclosure that content is machine-generated when disseminated publicly. Demucs output is described by the author as a grey area because of MUSDB training data.
results.hardware_notes: MiniMax Music 3 officially requires two CUDA GPUs (SGLang-Omni), so it cannot run on the Mac. ACE-Step 1.5 officially supports MPS/MLX on Apple Silicon, and the official acestep.cpp/acestep.vst3 run on Metal; lego, extract and complete need a base checkpoint (tutorial: xl-base at 12 GB or more). Demucs 4.0.1 supports MPS, with complex ops running on CPU. YuE2 is officially NVIDIA 24 GB only.

results.question: Under Suno's September-2026 ToS, may a Pro/Premier subscriber import their own downloaded Suno output (mix or Studio stems) into a local tool to (a) mix/master with DSP, (b) run local separation, (c) make generative edits or voice conversion, (d) release the result? Which clause governs, and what ownership do paid subscribers get?
results.finding:
These are the Terms of Service effective 2026-09-03, announced in Suno's blog on 2026-08-10.

Ownership: under 'Pro and Premier Accounts', 'Suno hereby assigns to you all of its right, title and interest in and to any Output owned by Suno and generated from Submissions made by you', 'provided such Output will remain subject to these Terms ... including any applicable commercial use restrictions'. Suno makes no warranty that copyright vests. Jon keeps all rights in his own Submissions, such as his melody and lyrics. Commercial use needs a permitted Download through an approved channel; stream ripping is prohibited. The assignment and Download rights are 'perpetual' and survive cancellation or downgrade. The use restrictions are 'contractual covenants', not carve-outs from the assigned rights. Free/Basic tier output is personal and non-commercial only. Remixes are joint works and non-commercial. Help-center articles agree: Pro/Premier songs are 'considered the owner' and keep commercial rights after the subscription ends.

(a) DSP mix/master: allowed. The governing text is 'You may edit, process, or convert the format of an Output you are otherwise permitted to use to the extent such use is incidental' (Permitted Commercial Use). The 'incidental' qualifier is undefined. Conventional DSP is not AI and is not caught by the AI clause.

(b) Local ML separation: grey. The governing clause is User Conduct item 'use the Services (and any Output or Voice Model) to create, develop or improve any competing products or services or to power, enable or train other artificial intelligence and machine learning models, tools or technologies'. Feeding Output to an ML separator can be read as 'enabling' an ML tool. No help article interprets this. The low-risk route is Suno's own stems: Pro has 'Auto; Split from mix' and Premier adds 'Advanced split'.

(c) Generative edits (ACE repaint/cover), voice conversion, or using the output to develop or test AURA: highest risk. The output becomes conditioning input to another AI model, which is the plain-language target of the 'power, enable or train' item. If AURA is or becomes a music-generation product, the separate covenant 'In no event will you use the Output ... to compete with Suno, including to create a competing music-generation product or service' also applies.

(d) Release: allowed for permitted Downloads of Pro/Premier output, 'solely to the extent it adheres to Suno's Conditions of Access and Use'. A DSP-finished release is fine. A release of an AI-edited derivative inherits the risk from (c). Suno's fingerprints, watermarks and metadata must not be removed or altered to conceal provenance.

No Suno help article addresses importing outputs into other AI tools.
results.corrected_value: AURA may be the DSP finishing tool (mix, master, format) for the paid Suno version, and the result may be released. ML separation of Suno audio is grey, so prefer Suno's own stems. Generative editing, cover, repaint or voice conversion of Suno audio, and any use of Suno audio to build or test AURA, should stay forbidden as D-11 rule 7 and D-21 already say, unless Jon accepts the ToS risk. Re-performing from Jon's own melody and lyrics, which are his Submissions, is unaffected.
results.output_rights: Pro/Premier: Suno assigns its rights in the Output; commercial use requires a permitted Download, is perpetual and survives cancellation; no copyright warranty; contractual use covenants (no AI powering or training, no competing) continue to apply.

results.question: (a) Is there independent human-preference/MOS evidence comparing VoxCPM2, Qwen3-TTS, Chatterbox, Fun-CosyVoice3 and Kokoro against ElevenLabs v3 / Multilingual v2 for long-form English narration? (b) Do ElevenLabs' ToS and Prohibited Use Policy allow existing ElevenLabs renders to be used as a cloning reference or as training data for another engine, and who keeps custom/PVC voices after the subscription ends?
results.finding:
(a) No independent long-form human-preference or MOS comparison exists for this set. Both arenas are short-form, blind, pairwise and English.

Artificial Analysis (no update date shown; newest entries Sep 2026): Eleven v3 1177 (4,679 samples); Multilingual v2 1095 (7,295); Kokoro 82M 1065 (5,296); Chatterbox (open) 1028 (4,641); Qwen3 TTS 932 and Qwen3 TTS Flash 944, which are Alibaba API entries and not confirmed to be the open checkpoint. VoxCPM, VoxCPM2, CosyVoice, Fun-CosyVoice3 and Chatterbox Turbo/Multilingual are absent. The board is topped by Eleven v4 Turbo (1329) and Eleven v4 (1326).

TTS Arena V2 (read from its /api/leaderboard; methodology says English-only, prompts up to 1,000 characters, 'Hear the same line'): Eleven Multilingual v2 1509±22 (1,143 votes); Eleven v3 1501±34 (547); Chatterbox 1481±19 (1,781; flagged not open, likely a hosted version); Kokoro v1.0 1478±22 (1,033; open, inactive). VoxCPM2, Qwen3-TTS and CosyVoice3 are absent.

The only independent long-form evidence is automatic metrics. arXiv 2609.16989, 'Taming Long-form TTS' (2026-09-15), reports that Qwen3-TTS and VoxCPM2 'significantly deteriorate' on prompts over 1,500 words. Qwen3-TTS-0.6B worst-of-10 WER is 35.2% without the authors' LACI method. Its authors are not affiliated with any of the vendors. Vendor reports (Qwen3-TTS, VoxCPM2) use their own test sets.

(b) No. The Prohibited Use Policy (Last Updated 17 August 2026), section 9, forbids: (j) 'Using any part of our Services or their Output to research and develop products, models, or services that compete with ElevenLabs'; (k) 'Using any part of our Services or their Output as input for any machine learning or training of artificial intelligence models'; and (l) using them 'as part of a dataset ... for training, fine-tuning, developing, testing, or improving any machine learning or artificial intelligence technology'. A zero-shot cloning reference is 'input for any machine learning', so Sabbath Echo's existing renders may be used neither as a reference nor as training data.

The Terms of Use (Last Updated 31 March 2026) say the user retains rights in Input (4(c)(i)) and Output (4(c)(ii)), but Output use stays subject to the Policy. The user grants ElevenLabs a perpetual, irrevocable licence to Content and to any User Voice Model (4(d)-(e)). The ToS do not state who owns a voice clone. Clones 'cannot download or export ... as standalone files'. On downgrade, a PVC 'will not be removed from your account, but you will not be able to use it until you upgrade to Creator or above'. After the subscription ends, 'you will still have a commercial license to use whatever you generated during that subscription forever'.
results.corrected_value: Narration quality versus ElevenLabs has to be measured in-house with long-form ASR/WER drift and blind listening; no external evidence settles it. Voice continuity for Sabbath Echo may only be seeded from the original human recordings (Jon's or a consenting narrator's Input), never from ElevenLabs renders. If the current voice is a Voice Library or Voice Design voice, it cannot legally be carried over by cloning.
results.output_rights: ElevenLabs: paid-plan output is commercial forever after the subscription ends, but may never be used as ML input, a training/test dataset, or to build competing models. Voice clones cannot be exported. A PVC is kept but unusable below the Creator tier.
results.hardware_notes: Not applicable. The arena scores are human-preference Elo for short prompts and cannot be used as speed or long-form claims.

new_discoveries: MiniMax API change (platform.minimax.io music-generation docs): from 2026-08-20 the paid Music and Lyrics Generation APIs are closed to new users, and the free models (music-3.0-free, music-2.6-free, music-cover-free) are discontinued. MiniMax points people to the open weights instead. Those weights officially need two CUDA GPUs, one for the Qwen3-8B AR model and one for Flow Matching/DAV, so they cannot run on the M5 Pro Mac. The 'LLC work on MiniMax' fallback therefore depends on Linux GPU specs that are still unknown.

MiniMax-Music3 Community License: commercial use is allowed, but commercial products must prominently show 'MiniMax-Music3' in their UI and need written authorization above US$20M yearly revenue. AUP item 11 requires clear disclosure when machine-generated content is disseminated publicly, which affects releases.

Demucs pretrained weights are not MIT. The author stated three times in official issues (#327, #384, #508) that they are research/personal-only, because MUSDB training data is research-only. On 2026-08-31 he removed 'license: mit' from the HF cards and export script (adefossez/demucs commit 2883f3db; HF commit 'Remove license from model card'). Demucs moves from 'unknown license' to non-commercial per the author, and an open-source-ready AURA needs a different default separator, for example ACE-Step 1.5 'extract' (MIT weights, generative) or a separator whose checkpoint licenses are verified.

YuE1 (YuE-v1 branch) weights are Apache-2.0 and it is the only engine in the set with native generation-time vocal and instrumental stems ('vtrack.mp3' and 'itrack.mp3'). It is a fully commercial, LLC-safe lane, but much weaker: SongBench Avg 4.92 versus 6.73 for YuE2 (YuE2 paper Table 2).

YuE2 now has a licensing contact split. The README (2026-09-17) lists 'Licensing inquiries: lauryliuyang@hkgai.org', while MODEL_LICENSE still names ryuanab@connect.ust.hk. The HF LICENSE files for YuE2-3B, Vae and Vae-legacy still carry plain CC BY-NC without the creator permission. A sole trader opened issue #219 on 2026-10-09 asking for commercial terms, so watch it for the first maintainer answer.

YuE2 source code auto-selects MPS and includes an MPS GQA attention fallback (src/yue2/pipeline.py line 135; modeling_yue2.py lines 21-24), even though the docs state Linux NVIDIA 24 GB only. A Mac YuE2 attempt is therefore plausible but unofficial and untested. Note also the official ComfyUI YuE2 nodes and NOIZ YuE2-Turbo (third-party) listed in the README.

ACE-Step has official Apple-native paths: the ACE-Step-1.5 README lists MLX for Apple Silicon, and the official ace-step/acestep.cpp and ace-step/acestep.vst3 (MIT, updated 2026-10-05) run on Metal and support lego. The official ACE-Step-DAW (WIP) implements a layer-by-layer 'LEGO pipeline' (drums, then bass, then guitar, then vocals), which matches AURA's stem and re-perform design.
ElevenLabs released Eleven v4 and v4 Turbo, now the top two on the Artificial Analysis TTS board (Elo 1326/1329, ahead of Eleven v3 at 1177). The narration replacement bar is now v4, not v3.

An independent long-form TTS paper (arXiv 2609.16989, 2026-09-15) shows Qwen3-TTS-0.6B and VoxCPM2 degrading badly beyond about 1,500 words: worst-of-10 WER is 35.2% and catastrophic failures (WER above 30%) occur in 26% of generations, falling to under 1% with its inference-only LACI method. The narration lane needs chunking plus ASR-based verify-and-regenerate as a core feature, not an add-on.

Suno ToS (effective 2026-09-03) contains an explicit allowance not in the current register: 'You may edit, process, or convert the format of an Output ... to the extent such use is incidental'. Use restrictions are framed as contractual covenants that survive cancellation, and Download-based commercial rights are perpetual. Download caps now apply: Pro 20 per month, Premier 60 per month, Studio workflows uncapped for Premier.
